generalizedRange: Central Asian steppe — reintroduced herds in Mongolia, northwest China and central Kazakhstan; most animals still in zoos and reserves worldwide
hook: Last seen wild in 1969. Every one alive descends from about a dozen horses.

story.text: Stocky and dun, with an upright mane like a zebra’s and no forelock, Przewalski’s horse is the only living horse never domesticated.
It has 66 chromosomes to the domestic horse’s 64, yet the two can still breed fertile foals.
The last wild one anyone recorded was seen in Mongolia’s Gobi in 1969; after that, only zoos.
By 1945 fewer than 20 breeding animals remained; every horse alive descends from about a dozen wild-caught founders.
On 5 June 1992, sixteen horses from the Netherlands were released at Hustai, Mongolia; the park now counts 380 in 34 harems.
The Gobi is harder ground: the dzud winter of 2022–23 killed about 180 of Great Gobi B’s 400-odd horses.
At China’s Kalamaili reserve, released horses starved their first winter and were corralled each cold season; by 2013 about 121 lived there, most wild-born.
In June 2024 Czech Air Force planes carried seven horses to Kazakhstan’s Altyn Dala, absent some 200 years; the first steppe-born foal came in August 2026.
In August 2020 a foal named Kurt was born to a domestic mare in Texas, cloned from cells frozen in 1980 — genes the herd had lost.
To witness the Przewalski’s horse is to watch a species walk out of a studbook onto three countries’ steppe — and to know how thin that line is.

stats.size: Up to 5 ft at the withers · 550–800 lbs (250–360 kg)
stats.lifespan: About 18 years on average; up to 36 recorded
stats.diet: Grazer — wild grasses, plus leaves of shrubs

reproduction.text: One foal after about eleven months, born at roughly 66 pounds; mares breed from around three years, stallions from five.

insight.text: Przewalski’s horse has 66 chromosomes and the domestic horse 64 — yet unlike a mule, their 65-chromosome hybrid is fertile.

habitatRegions.name: Great Gobi B, Dzungarian Gobi, western Mongolia

programs.title: Return of the Wild Horses, Kazakhstan
programs.summary: Keeper of the species’ international studbook since 1959, Prague Zoo flies about eight horses a year from European zoos to the Alibi centre on Kazakhstan’s Altyn Dala, holds them a year in acclimatisation enclosures, and releases them — aiming for some 40 horses by 2028.

programs.title: Takhi reintroduction, Great Gobi B
programs.summary: Runs the reintroduction in Mongolia’s Great Gobi B Strictly Protected Area — transports since 1992, ranger monitoring of harems and bachelor groups, and rebuilding the herd after dzud winters — toward a long-term goal of 1,000 breeding animals.
